description: Make Agent archive reversible end-to-end (server grain + API unarchive route, web client/mutation, detail-page Unarchive affordance, honest confirmation text) and surface archived agents in the already-shipped Archived list section, while aligning the detail-page Actions card button with its label.

tasks.title: Server: UnarchiveAsync grain + POST unarchive API route (symmetric to archive)
tasks.description: Add the server-side reverse lifecycle symmetric to archive. Extend `IAgentGrain` with `UnarchiveAsync` (alongside `ArchiveAsync`) and implement it in `AgentGrain` to set `Status = Active`, advance `UpdatedAt`, and persist — mirroring `ArchiveAsync` (`AgentGrain.cs:80-87`) but following D2/D3: return `Task<AgentInfo?>` (null for not-found, matching the agent archive contract, not the Issue throw shape) and short-circuit as an idempotent no-op (return `AgentQuerier.ToInfo(_agent)` without bumping `UpdatedAt` or persisting) when the agent is already active. Add `POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/agents/{id}/unarchive` on `AgentDefinitionRoutes` mirroring the DELETE archive route's `result is null ? NotFound : Ok(result)` shape (D1, D4); leave DELETE (archive) and PATCH (unchanged, `status` stays out of `GetFields`) untouched. Follow the Issue domain precedent (`IssueRoutes.Lifecycle.cs:160`, `IIssueGrain.UnarchiveAsync`) only as a shape reference.
acceptanceCriteria: IAgentGrain exposes UnarchiveAsync returning Task<AgentInfo?>, symmetric to ArchiveAsync
AgentGrain.UnarchiveAsync transitions an archived agent to Status=active, advances UpdatedAt to the current time, and persists the change
Archive then unarchive round-trips an agent back to active status (verified by a grain unit test)
Unarchive of an already-active agent is a deterministic no-op: returns the active AgentInfo without advancing UpdatedAt and without persisting (no unhandled exception, no state corruption)
Unarchive of an unknown agent id returns null (not-found), matching the archive path's contract, and does not create or mutate any agent
POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/agents/{id}/unarchive returns 200 with the unarchived AgentInfo (status=active) for an archived agent, and 404 for an unknown agent
DELETE /{id} continues to perform archive and PATCH /{id} continues to ignore any status field (regression-covered by existing or extended API spec tests)
Grain unit tests pass (round-trip, already-active no-op, unknown null) and API spec tests pass on the new route; dotnet build is clean (TreatWarningsAsErrors) and the full server test suite passes
tasks.output: Server code change (IAgentGrain, AgentGrain, AgentDefinitionRoutes) plus passing grain unit + API spec coverage for the unarchive lifecycle; the route is callable before any web work begins
tasks.notes: Foundational server task; the web tasks (T-002+) depend on the route existing. No schema migration — Status/active/archived already exist (Agent.cs:20-24) and AgentInfo already carries status on the wire. Orleans single-activation per grain key serializes concurrent archive/unarchive calls, so no extra locking is needed. No dependencies: this is the root of the DAG.

tasks.title: Web data layer: unarchive client + mutation, and archived-agent list visibility
tasks.description: Wire the web data layer for unarchive and populate the dormant Archived list section. (1) Add `unarchiveAgent(projectId, id)` next to `archiveAgent` (`client.ts:81`) issuing `POST .../agents/{id}/unarchive` expecting `request<AgentInfo>` (D4). (2) Add `useUnarchiveAgent` next to `useArchiveAgent` (`queries.ts:102`) with `onSuccess` invalidating both `['agents']` and `['agent-status']` (D7 — mirroring useArchiveAgent at queries.ts:108-109 so the runner re-evaluates the agent) plus a success toast (lean wording 'Agent restored'). Export both `unarchiveAgent` and `useUnarchiveAgent` from the agent entity barrel (`index.ts`). (3) Visibility fix (D5): change `useAgents` (`queries.ts:54-61`) to call `listAgents(projectId!, { all: true })` so the existing Archived section renders, then filter the one other consumer that must show only launchable agents — `AgentSessionComposerPage` (`.../AgentSessionComposerPage.tsx:161`) — to `agents?.filter((a) => a.status !== 'archived')`. Keep a single `['agents']` cache key (no useAllAgents split).
acceptanceCriteria: unarchiveAgent(projectId, id) client function issues POST to the agent's /unarchive route and is exported from the agent entity barrel
useUnarchiveAgent mutation is exported from the barrel and its onSuccess invalidates both ['agents'] and ['agent-status'] (mirroring useArchiveAgent), and shows a success toast
useAgents calls listAgents with { all: true }, so archived agents are included in the query result and the ['agents'] cache key remains unified

AgentSessionComposerPage filters its agent picker to status !== 'archived', so archived agents do not appear as launchable in the session launcher (the server's archived-cannot-launch invariant is preserved as a backstop)
client.test.ts covers unarchiveAgent issuing the POST; queries.test.ts covers useUnarchiveAgent cache invalidation (['agents'] and ['agent-status']) and useAgents passing all:true
A composer test covers an archived agent not appearing in the launcher picker

A list-page component test covers the agent-archive spec's Archived section scenarios: archived agents appear in the 'Archived (n)' section (count matches), archived rows render visually distinct and remain navigable into the detail page, and the section is omitted when no archived agents exist
Web typecheck passes (npm run typecheck -w packages/web) and web tests pass (npm run test:run -w packages/web)
tasks.output: Web entity changes (client.ts, queries.ts, index.ts) plus composer filter, with passing client/queries/composer tests; the unarchive mutation and archived list data are consumable by the UI tasks
tasks.notes: Depends on T-001: unarchiveAgent calls POST /{id}/unarchive, which only exists after T-001 ships the route. The visibility (all:true) part does not itself depend on T-001 (AgentQuerier already supports the all param), but it is co-located in queries.ts with the mutation and ships in the same task to keep the web data layer coherent. D5 rejects a useAgents/useAllAgents split because fragmenting the ['agents'] cache risks stale archived state. Blast radius of all:true is known and small: AgentSessionComposerPage is the only other consumer that must show active-only; AgentListPage already has the Archived section and detail page consumers already handle archived rows. Audit any other useAgents consumers while editing.

tasks.title: Detail page Actions card: direct-trigger Archive (active) + Unarchive control (archived)
tasks.description: Resolve the Actions card label/behavior mismatch (issue problem 2) and close the unarchive UI loop (D6). (1) For an ACTIVE agent, the misleading 'Archive' button (`AgentDetailPage.tsx:284-294`, testid `agent-detail-archive-btn`) now triggers archive directly via `useArchiveAgent` with its own local confirm step (local `archiveConfirmOpen` state, reusing the destructive-confirm pattern already in `AgentProfileEditor.tsx:251-275`) — it SHALL NOT merely open the Edit dialog. The testid stays but now behaves as its label promises. (2) For an ARCHIVED agent, replace the static 'This agent is archived and cannot be launched.' notice (`AgentDetailPage.tsx:295-298`) with an actionable 'Unarchive'/'Restore' control bound to `useUnarchiveAgent`. (3) Keep the top-level Edit button (`AgentDetailPage.tsx:177-185`) as the canonical edit entry, and keep 'New Session' disabled for archived agents (spec: archived agents cannot start new sessions — preserved, not regressed).
acceptanceCriteria: For an active agent, the Actions 'Archive' button (testid agent-detail-archive-btn) initiates the archive flow (confirmation then archive) directly and does NOT open the Edit dialog as its sole side effect
The direct-trigger archive uses a confirm step (local state), reusing the destructive-confirm affordance pattern; cancelling the confirm does not archive
For an archived agent, the static archived notice is replaced by an Unarchive/Restore control in the Actions card, bound to useUnarchiveAgent

After unarchive from the detail page, the agent re-appears in the Active list group and leaves the Archived group (covered by a detail/list interaction test or by the cache invalidation in T-002 plus a component assertion)
After unarchive, the detail-page 'New Session' control becomes enabled for that agent (archived-cannot-launch invariant correctly relaxes on return to active)
For an archived agent, the 'New Session' control remains disabled (no regression of the archived-cannot-launch behavior)
Detail-page component tests cover: active-agent direct archive with confirm, archived-agent Unarchive control, and no remaining label/behavior mismatch
Web typecheck and tests pass
tasks.output: AgentDetailPage Actions card rewrite (direct archive for active + Unarchive control for archived) plus passing detail-page component tests
tasks.notes: Depends on T-002: the Unarchive control binds to useUnarchiveAgent (delivered in T-002); the direct-trigger archive reuses the destructive-confirm pattern but invokes useArchiveAgent which is pre-existing, so only the unarchive half strictly depends on T-002. Sequenced after T-002 to avoid editing the detail page against a moving data-layer contract. D6 chose direct-trigger over removal so the Actions card stays useful for active agents; the Edit-dialog archive entry (AgentProfileEditor) remains available regardless. This task touches AgentDetailPage for both capabilities (archive button honesty + unarchive control) to keep the Actions card a single coherent module per design D6.

tasks.title: Honest archive confirmation dialog text in AgentProfileEditor
tasks.description: Rewrite the lying confirmation copy (D8). The current `DialogDescription` (`AgentProfileEditor.tsx:255-258`) promises the agent 'will remain visible' and 'can be reversed' — both unbacked pre-fix. Rewrite it to state the real effect: the agent leaves the Active group and cannot start new sessions. Because unarchive now exists end-to-end (T-001..T-003), the text MAY honestly state the action is reversible from the agent detail page. Drop the vague 'remain visible' claim and the unbacked 'can be reversed' promise; any reversibility wording must be backed by the detail-page Unarchive affordance delivered in T-003 (spec scenario: reversibility claim backed by a working affordance).
acceptanceCriteria: The archive confirmation DialogDescription states the real effect: the agent leaves the Active group and cannot start new sessions
The description does NOT contain the pre-fix 'remain visible' phrasing or an unbacked 'can be reversed' promise

Any reversibility claim in the dialog is backed by a reachable Unarchive affordance on the agent detail page (delivered in T-003) — satisfying the spec's 'reversibility claim is backed by a working affordance' scenario
A component test asserts the confirmation dialog text matches archive's actual effect and contains neither pre-fix false phrase
Web typecheck and tests pass
tasks.output: AgentProfileEditor confirmation text rewrite plus a passing component test asserting honest copy
tasks.notes: Depends on T-003: the core fix (removing false claims) is text-only and independent, but the spec permits honestly stating reversibility only when a working unarchive affordance exists; the detail-page affordance lands in T-003, so T-004 is sequenced after it so every task boundary leaves the reversibility claim truthful. If the chosen wording omits any reversibility claim, this task could run in parallel with T-003; it is sequenced last only to keep the 'reversible from the detail page' phrasing honest at every commit. Small, self-contained edit.
